notes: Strong T1, but T10-T11 and T17-T18 were spent clicking for credits on 15-24 credits with nothing to spend them on, and the runner declined to pay 2 for Loot Box on T12 and T19 despite being rich. The decisive mistake came at 6 points on T20-T21: the runner ran the N-Pot Server 2 twice instead of the Server 1 card being advanced, which was Freedom of Information, the corp's winning agenda and a steal that would have won the game.

R&D was left open until T5 and lost three agendas, and T2's ice went on HQ instead. With 11-17 credits from T10-T21 the corp mostly clicked for credits and advanced Servers 3 and 4 one counter a turn, never scoring again after T4. It also left Project Yagi-Uda in unprotected Archives, which the runner took on T21 for the win.

Reached 5 points on T1, then ignored the advanced Server 1 card (Above the Law) on T3 and the card there on T5, repeatedly running R&D or clicking credits when either steal would have won. From T10-T16 the runner sat on 19-37 credits clicking for credits while the corp installed and advanced in Server 1 on T14 and T16, and lost at 6 points.

Clean game: Ansel 1.0 on R&D wrecked the runner's rig, campaigns and Otto clicks kept money flowing, and both Méliès City Luxury Line scores were set up well (Seamless Launch fast-advance on T10). The only oddity was spending 6 credits rezzing Ansel on Server 2 on T5 to protect an Otto Campaign.

Fast, efficient aggression: Concerto and plain runs on an open HQ, then Jailbreak with Docklands Pass and Bravado on T4, won by T4. The one risk was carrying up to 4 tags (Oppo Research, Behold!) on T3-T4 with Game Over in HQ, though the corp was broke.

No ice on HQ or R&D until T3/T4 while playing Petty Cash and drawing on 10-14 credits, which handed the runner two Megaprix Qualifiers and Architect Deployment Test. On T9-T11, holding 21-29 credits and 7-8 cards, the corp just clicked for credits and never added a second ice to the single-Wave R&D, which lost Méliès City Luxury Line on T11.

Good early R&D pressure on a mostly open corp, which won by T7. Tag handling was loose: the runner stayed tagged from Oracle Thinktank on T2-T4 (even with 10 credits on T4) and installed resources like Daily Casts that the corp trashed on T3 and T7.

Checked remotes sensibly and broke Server 4 (Ballista, Descent) for Above the Law on T13/T14 and Divested Trust on T18/T26. Otherwise, from about T7 the runner clicked for credits nearly every turn, reaching 58 credits by T25, and never pressured HQ or R&D while sitting at 5-6 points, which dragged the game to T26.

The trap remotes (Urtica Cipher x3, Esca, Bladderworts via Mitosis) worked well early, but HQ kept a single Semak-samun that Rising Tide broke every turn. On T13 and T15 the corp iced empty remotes instead of HQ and lost Lotus Haze (T13) and See How They Run (T16) from HQ. Longevity Serum emptied HQ and left the corp on 1 credit on T11-T12.

Scored Sisyphus Protocol and Hybrid Releases cheaply and closed with a good net-damage flatline using Anemone, Bathynomus and Sisyphus re-encounters on T17-T18. However, See How They Run (T15) and Regenesis (T16) went into Server 6 behind a single Hafrún the runner could break, with 10-13 credits unused, and T8 and T11 were all clicks for credits.

Tagging (Oppo Research on T2 and T11, Public Trail on T5 and T13) had no follow-up even with 13 credits, and T11 used only one click. The economy then sagged to 1-4 credits on T14-T18, and only 4 points were scored in 20 turns. Server 2 was built up to four ice, but R&D with two ice lost Next Big Thing on T20.

Good start: Banner got SDS Drone Deployment on T2 and the Ballista trade for Above the Law on T3 put the runner on 5 points. On T5-T6, with 8-13 credits, the runner did not run the Server 1 card that the corp (at 0-3 credits) could not defend, and the corp scored Divested Trust from it on T7. Later the runner never found a barrier breaker for Akhet, spent T10-T11 clicking for credits, and on T17 ran Archives instead of advanced Server 2.

Built a three-ice Server 1, but after the runner got through on T5 the corp kept feeding agendas into it: Embedded Reporting on T6 with 1 credit and Next Big Thing on T7, advanced twice on 0 credits. The runner, already at 6 points, simply walked in on T8. T3 was three clicks for credits, and spending 2 credits to trash Daily Casts on T6 left nothing to defend with.

Tread Lightly found Fujii Asset Retrieval on T1, and Revolver through Karunā took two Project Yagi-Udas from Server 2. However, on T7, T9, T11 and T12 the runner clicked for credits on 10-31 credits while the corp advanced Server 1 and Hybrid Release put a card in a fresh remote. With Docklands Pass installed, HQ was never run all game.

Kept steady pressure: broke Vampyronassa with Shibboleth for Hybrid Release on T5, took Project Yagi-Uda with Jailbreak and Docklands Pass on T6, tanked net damage for Regenesis on T7, and checked Archives after Hansei Review to win with Fujii on T11. Running the twice-advanced naked Server 1 into Urtica Cipher on T2 cost four cards but was a defensible read.

R&D was open on T1 and lost Architect Deployment Test. Superconducting Hub then went into Server 2 behind one Hagen and was stolen on T3. HQ was flooded with two Project Ingatans and Méliès behind only Vertigo, yet T4 and T5 went to Sprint, Hedge Fund and remote installs instead of more HQ ice, and the runner took Ingatan on T4 and Méliès on T5.

Exploited a broke Weyland corp well: Buzzsaw through Descent for Transport Monopoly on T5, a run on unrezzed Server 1 for Above the Law, and repeated HQ runs. Several T6-T7 HQ runs hit ZATO City Grid again rather than trashing it with spare credits, and Trickster Taka's tags cost The Twinning three times.

The economy collapsed to 0-3 credits from T3 on, so agendas sat unadvanced in Server 1 behind Karunā. The runner tanked the damage and stole Project Yagi-Uda (T3) and Sericulture Expansion (T5 and T7). R&D was left with unrezzable ice and lost Flower Sermon on T6, the T2 ice went on an empty Server 2, and AU Co. draws forced 2-card discards on T5-T6.

Strong game: Drafter and two Ansel 1.0 on R&D shredded the rig, a campaign engine with repeated Hedge Funds funded everything, and Wage Workers clicks scored Ingatan (T10) and ADT (T11). ADT then put Méliès naked into Server 11. On T12 the corp used Seamless Launch but spent its other clicks on Sprint and Hedge Funds instead of advancing out, giving the runner a turn at a naked 3-pointer.

Good T11, stealing Remastered Edition through three ice and Kingmaking from HQ to reach 5 points. Apart from that, T6, T8-T10 and T12-T18 were almost all clicks for credits, reaching 25 credits without running HQ or R&D, even though HQ had just yielded an agenda. The winning Kingmaking was in HQ and only taken on T20.
